title: Atomic CRUD Atlas
content:
Complete integration example using Atlas ORM for high-speed database orchestration within Photon routes. Atlas provides a Laravel Eloquent-like Active Record pattern with zero overhead.

Defining a Model

Start by defining your model class:

import { Model, column } from '@gravito/atlas'

class Project extends Model {
  // Define table name
  static table = 'projects'
  
  // Primary key (defaults to 'id')
  static primaryKey = 'id'

  // Define columns with @column decorator
  @column({ isPrimary: true })
  declare id: number

  @column()
  declare title: string

  @column()
  declare description: string

  @column()
  declare active: boolean

  @column()
  declare created_at: Date

  @column()
  declare updated_at: Date
}

Create (Insert)

1

Using new + save()

const project = new Project()
project.title = 'New Project'
project.description = 'Description'
project.active = true
await project.save()
2

Using create()

const project = await Project.create({
  title: 'New Project',
  description: 'Description',
  active: true
})

Read (Query)

Basic Queries

// Find by ID
const project = await Project.find(1)

// Find first matching record
const project = await Project.where('active', true).first()

// Get all records
const projects = await Project.all()

// Get multiple records with conditions
const projects = await Project
  .where('active', true)
  .orderBy('created_at', 'desc')
  .limit(10)
  .get()

Advanced Queries

// Complex where clauses
const projects = await Project.query()
  .where('active', true)
  .where('created_at', '>', new Date('2024-01-01'))
  .whereIn('id', [1, 2, 3])
  .orderBy('id', 'desc')
  .get()

// Search with LIKE
const projects = await Project
  .where('title', 'like', '%keyword%')
  .get()

// Aggregates
const count = await Project.where('active', true).count()
const total = await Project.sum('views')
const avg = await Project.avg('rating')

Update

1

Modify + save()

const project = await Project.find(1)
if (project) {
  project.title = 'Updated Title'
  await project.save()
}
2

Using update()

const project = await Project.find(1)
if (project) {
  await project.update({
    title: 'Updated Title',
    active: false
  })
}
3

Mass Update

await Project
  .where('active', false)
  .update({ status: 'archived' })

Delete

1

Single Delete

const project = await Project.find(1)
if (project) {
  await project.delete()
}
2

Bulk Delete

await Project
  .where('active', false)
  .delete()

Complete Photon Route Example

Full CRUD API

Complete RESTful API implementation with Atlas ORM.

import { Photon } from '@gravito/photon'
import { Project } from './models/Project'

const app = new Photon()

// GET /projects - List all projects
app.get('/projects', async (c) => {
  const page = parseInt(c.req.query('page') || '1')
  const perPage = parseInt(c.req.query('per_page') || '10')
  
  const result = await Project.query()
    .where('active', true)
    .orderBy('created_at', 'desc')
    .paginate(perPage, page)
  
  return c.json({
    data: result.data,
    pagination: result.pagination
  })
})

// GET /projects/:id - Get single project
app.get('/projects/:id', async (c) => {
  const id = parseInt(c.req.param('id'))
  const project = await Project.find(id)
  
  if (!project) {
    return c.json({ error: 'Project not found' }, 404)
  }
  
  return c.json({ project })
})

// POST /projects - Create new project
app.post('/projects', async (c) => {
  const body = await c.req.json()
  
  const project = await Project.create({
    title: body.title,
    description: body.description,
    active: body.active ?? true
  })
  
  return c.json({ project }, 201)
})

// PUT /projects/:id - Update project
app.put('/projects/:id', async (c) => {
  const id = parseInt(c.req.param('id'))
  const body = await c.req.json()
  
  const project = await Project.find(id)
  if (!project) {
    return c.json({ error: 'Project not found' }, 404)
  }
  
  await project.update({
    title: body.title,
    description: body.description,
    active: body.active
  })
  
  return c.json({ project })
})

// DELETE /projects/:id - Delete project
app.delete('/projects/:id', async (c) => {
  const id = parseInt(c.req.param('id'))
  
  const project = await Project.find(id)
  if (!project) {
    return c.json({ error: 'Project not found' }, 404)
  }
  
  await project.delete()
  
  return c.json({ message: 'Project deleted' })
})

Relationships

Define relationships in your models:

// User Model
class User extends Model {
  static table = 'users'
  
  // One-to-Many: User has many Posts
  posts() {
    return this.hasMany(Post, 'user_id')
  }
}

// Post Model
class Post extends Model {
  static table = 'posts'
  
  // Many-to-One: Post belongs to User
  user() {
    return this.belongsTo(User, 'user_id')
  }
  
  // Many-to-Many: Post has many Tags
  tags() {
    return this.belongsToMany(Tag, 'post_tags', 'post_id', 'tag_id')
  }
}

// Usage with eager loading
const user = await User.query()
  .with('posts')
  .find(1)

console.log(user.posts) // Array of Post models

Transactions

Data Integrity

Use transactions to ensure data consistency across multiple operations.

import { DB } from '@gravito/atlas'

await DB.transaction(async (trx) => {
  // Create project
  const project = await Project.create({
    title: 'New Project',
    active: true
  })
  
  // Create related records
  await Task.create({
    project_id: project.id,
    title: 'First Task'
  })
  
  // If any operation fails, all changes are rolled back
})

Pagination

// Simple pagination
const result = await Project.query()
  .where('active', true)
  .paginate(10, 1) // perPage, page

// Result structure:
// {
//   data: [...],
//   pagination: {
//     total: 100,
//     perPage: 10,
//     page: 1,
//     lastPage: 10
//   }
// }

return c.json(result)

Best Practices

  • ✓
    Use Eager LoadingUse .with() to prevent N+1 query problems
  • ✓
    Use TransactionsWrap related operations in transactions for data integrity
  • ✓
    Validate InputAlways validate request data before database operations
  • ✓
    Handle ErrorsUse try-catch blocks and return appropriate HTTP status codes
  • ✓
    Use Query BuilderFor complex queries, use the fluent query builder API

Performance: Atlas is built with the same "No-Shim" philosophy as Photon. It uses direct dynamic driver loading and pre-compiled query templates, making it significantly faster than Prisma or TypeORM in high-load scenarios. The Active Record pattern provides an elegant API while maintaining zero overhead.
